tagline: Sign-in and sharing are self-serve, but almost everything else sits behind partner-program approval.
summary: LinkedIn offers exactly three self-serve OAuth products - Sign in with LinkedIn (OpenID Connect: profile, email) and Share on LinkedIn (posting for a member). Everything else - Marketing/Advertising API, Sales Navigator, talent integrations - requires approval through a partner program, and compliance APIs are closed entirely. Creating any app also requires associating it with a LinkedIn Page and having the Page admin verify the association, which solo builders without a company page often trip over.

difficulty.label: Moderate
difficulty.rationale: Scoped to the open self-serve products (member sign-in and share): registration is quick but has the Page-verification hoop and a very narrow permission set. If your agent needs advertising, sales, or recruiting data, this becomes a 5 - gated partner programs with business-case review.

timeToFirstToken: About 30-60 minutes for Sign in with LinkedIn once your app is created and Page-verified: add the product in the Developer Portal, configure the redirect URL, run the standard OIDC authorization-code flow.

approvalWait.label: Page admin verification (days); partner programs (weeks+, case-by-case)
approvalWait.detail: The app must be associated with a LinkedIn Page, and verification is confirmed by a Page admin - fast if you control the Page, a real blocker if you do not. Open products are usable immediately after that. Marketing API access requires applying to the partner program; Sales Navigator requires SNAP partnership; talent products require their own program applications. LinkedIn does not publish review SLAs for these.

steps.title: Create the app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal
steps.detail: developer.linkedin.com -> Create app. You must name a LinkedIn Page as the app's publisher - create a Page first if you have none.

steps.title: Verify the Page association
steps.detail: Generate the verification URL in the app's settings and have a Page admin open it to confirm. Apps are permanently associated with the Page.

steps.title: Add products on the Products tab
steps.detail: Self-serve: 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' (profile, email scopes) and 'Share on LinkedIn' (w_member_social). Everything else shows an application/approval path.

steps.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 redirect URLs and run OIDC
steps.detail: Standard authorization-code flow against linkedin.com/oauth/v2 endpoints; request only the scopes your products grant.

steps.title: (Only if needed) Apply to a partner program
steps.detail: Marketing API, SNAP, or talent programs each have their own application and review; plan for business-case questions and no guaranteed timeline.

requirements: A personal LinkedIn account in good standing (human step).
A LinkedIn Page whose admin will verify the app association - the association is permanent.
An HTTPS redirect URL for the OAuth flow.
For anything beyond sign-in/share: an approved partner-program application with a business case.
nuances: The legacy r_liteprofile and r_emailaddress permissions were replaced by OpenID Connect scopes - older tutorials referencing them are outdated.
w_member_social (posting) is self-serve, which surprises people who assume all write access is gated.
There is no general API to read members' profiles or connections - those live in closed/partner products.
Compliance (archiving) APIs are closed and cannot be requested at all.
Page association is permanent: choose a Page you will keep, not a throwaway.
agentCanDo: Map your feature list to LinkedIn's product table and tell you immediately whether it is self-serve or partner-gated.
Draft the OIDC integration code and the exact redirect configuration.
Prepare the partner-program application narrative if you need gated APIs.
humanMustDo: Own the LinkedIn account and the Page, and complete Page verification.
Accept LinkedIn's API terms and any partner-program agreements.
Correspond with LinkedIn during partner review.

evidence.claim: Only three permissions are open to all developers without special approval: profile and email (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) and w_member_social (Share on LinkedIn); 'Most permissions and partner programs require explicit approval from LinkedIn.'

Advertising API access requires approval via the Developer Portal; Sales Navigator access requires SNAP partnership; talent integrations require applying to their programs; Compliance permissions are closed.
Apps must be associated with a LinkedIn Page that acts as the app's publisher; for certain functionality an app verification request must be confirmed by the Page.
Requirements and gating were read from LinkedIn/Microsoft pages on 2026-10-28; no LinkedIn app was created and no partner application was submitted for this take-home.

uncertainties: LinkedIn publishes no review timelines for partner programs; community reports range from days to months.
The exact set of open products changes over time - the Products tab of a live app is authoritative.
The developer portal itself requires sign-in, so the live registration flow was not exercised end-to-end.
